1.0: QUESTION: What is the fundamental nature of consciousness?
1.1: ASSERTS: Three major theoretical frameworks compete to explain consciousness: emergentism, panpsychism, and alternative approaches
1.2: ASSERTS: Consciousness intimately connected to neural activity - brain damage reliably affects conscious experience
1.3: OPEN: Explanatory gap between objective neural processes and subjective experience persists
1.4: ASSERTS: Emergentism currently aligns best with scientific methodology and empirical findings
1.1.1: ASSERTS: Emergentist view holds consciousness arises from complex neural network interactions, like wetness emerging from H2O molecules
1.1.2: ASSERTS: Panpsychist position treats consciousness as fundamental feature of reality like mass or electric charge
1.1.3: DOCUMENT: Alternative frameworks include Integrated Information Theory, quantum theories, and illusionist approaches
1.2.1: ASSERTS: Neuroscientific interventions can alter subjective states in predictable ways
1.2.2: OPEN: Correlation doesn't resolve whether consciousness emerges from neural complexity or neural activity modulates underlying conscious substrate
1.4.1: OPEN: Hard problem remains genuinely difficult rather than merely conceptually confused
1.4.2: OPEN: Question may require conceptual breakthroughs comparable to physics or may point to fundamental limits in human understanding
1.1.1.1: ASSERTS: Proponents include Daniel Dennett and Patricia Churchland who argue sufficient neural complexity naturally produces subjective experience
1.1.1.2: ASSERTS: Neuroscientific findings show strong correlations between specific brain states and conscious experiences
1.1.1.3: ASSERTS: Consciousness appears dependent on neural integrity
1.1.1.4: REJECTS: Emergentism fails to solve the 'hard problem of consciousness' - unclear why subjective experience exists rather than mere unconscious processing
1.1.2.1: ASSERTS: Advocates include David Chalmers and Galen Strawson
1.1.2.2: ASSERTS: All matter possesses rudimentary conscious experience; human consciousness represents complex organization of basic conscious properties
1.1.2.3: ASSERTS: Sidesteps hard problem by denying consciousness emerges from non-conscious components
1.1.2.4: REJECTS: Faces 'combination problem' - unclear how micro-experiences combine into unified macro-consciousness
1.1.2.5: REJECTS: Struggles with empirical testability and counterintuitive attribution of consciousness to rocks and electrons
1.1.3.1: ASSERTS: Integrated Information Theory proposes consciousness corresponds to integrated information processing with mathematical measurement tools
1.1.3.2: REJECTS: IIT raises questions about counterintuitive implications
1.1.3.3: ASSERTS: Quantum theories suggest consciousness involves quantum processes in neural microtubules
1.1.3.4: REJECTS: Quantum theories remain highly speculative and lack strong empirical support
1.1.3.5: ASSERTS: Illusionist approaches argue consciousness is compelling cognitive illusion
1.1.3.6: REJECTS: Illusionism seems to deny rather than explain the phenomenon
